# Review — cid-tiradas-128-130 (vv. 2675–2762, tiradas 128–130)

Checked: every unit's `t`/`l`/`i`/`n` (33 units) against the pinned packet and conventions.md; the scan, PDF pp. 299–304
(printed 295–300), read on the image, including the three tirada rubrics and every Pidal footnote on these pages (2683,
2687, 2692, 2693, 2697, 2698, 2703, 2707, 2711, 2713, 2720, 2721, 2729, 2731, 2732, 2733, 2743, 2746, 2750, 2752, 2754,
2759-60, 2761), with zoom-5 strips of Ati[en]ça (2691) and nu[ov]es (2698). There is no footnote to 2685, 2694, 2695,
2696, 2705, 2725, 2728, 2736, 2753 or 2756. Cross-references checked in the published parts: v. 415 (Miedes, Atienza on
the Çid's right), vv. 2280 ff. (the lion breaks loose, published 2280–2282), vv. 2564 and 2570 (arras), vv. 2079–2081
(*que sean rogadores*, the king's speech; *dándoslas* = dadnos las), v. 832 *indos* = idnos, v. 2575 (Colada and Tizón
given to the Infantes), v. 2671 *barragán*, v. 2673 *armas iva teniendo*, v. 2653 *troçir*, v. 2388 *ensayarse*, v. 396
"San Esteban", v. 172 *Grádanse*, the many *recabdo* lines (vv. 23 … 1741), and the glossary's *dexás*, *sonás*,
*desenparás* (apocopated imperfect subjunctives). Pass 2 covered all 95 new gloss entries and the `__broaden__` block,
with old entries taken from known-forms.json, and the known forms of this part for senses they do not cover.

All three rubrics match the print (128: the six-clause rubric; 129: *Los infantes abandonan a sus mujeres. (Serie
gemela.)*; 130: *Los infantes se alaban de su cobardía*). The `t` fields joined by "\n" equal the packet's 82 verses in
order (2675–2676 printed at the head of 128, after 2680; 2754-5 and 2759-60 one line each, *rogados* overflowing to the
end of 2761 on the image, as the note says); no `t` was changed; every `l` has as many lines as its `t` (verified by
script after editing).

## Pass 1: units.json

1. 2686–2688 · n · weak. Pidal's note to v. 2687 was quoted with the quotation closed after its first clause, so his
   own comment ('Por esta parte … vado') stood outside it. Now one quotation, his quoted gloss in inner double quotes
   (as in the 126–127 review).
2. 2731–2733 · n · weak. Same fault in the note to v. 2733 ('os lo demandarán en vistas o cortes'. Las vistas, …
   cortes'). Fixed the same way.
3. 2731–2733 · n · weak. Pidal's 'os envileceréis a vosotros mismos' was put as "you would debase yourselves"; it is a
   future. Now "you will debase yourselves".
4. 2759–2762 · n · weak. Same quotation fault in the note to v. 2761 ('pues no eran …'. Pareja … 2333'). Fixed.
5. 2759–2762 · i, n · weak. *assís irá vengando* was "So the dishonour of the lion is being avenged" — the future
   *irá* was lost. `i` now "Thus shall the dishonour of the lion be avenged."; the note says assís = assí + se, the se
   making the line passive, ir + gerund of a thing done step by step, future.
6. 2737–2740 · l · weak. *ronpien* (imperfect; the note says so) was "they-tore". Now "they-were-tearing". `i` keeps
   "they tore".
7. 2722–2723 · n · error. "duradores … with its e before the s for the ó-e assonance" is wrong: -es is the ordinary
   plural. Now: an adjective in -dor with one form for both genders, here with feminine *çinchas* (as *tajadores* with
   *espadas*, v. 2726); its plural -ores gives the ó-e.
8. 2747–2748 · n · weak. "said again at the end of the next tirada (v. 2752)": v. 2752 is the last line but one of 129
   (Pidal, note to 2754: 'semejante al penúltimo de la serie anterior'). Corrected.
9. 2754–2756 · l, n · weak. *nol torna recabdo* was "not-her gives care": *nol* = non + le is dative ('to her') and
   *torna* is 'returns'. Now "not-to-her returns heed"; the note says le takes up *al otra* and gives the literal
   'returns heed'. The sense ('neither could tend to or answer the other') stays marked as from context.
10. 2726–2728 · n · style. *cortandos* = cortadnos: Pidal has no note here; the published parallels *dándoslas* =
    dadnos las (v. 2081) and *indos* = idnos (v. 832) are now cited, with a word on why not a gerund.
11. 2752–2753 · n · style. *assomas*: now said to be 3rd sg. imperfect subjunctive with the stress left on the a
    (assomás, printed without accent), as *fincás* v. 2709, echoing *que assomasse* v. 2742.
12. 2759–2762 · n · style. *deviemos* "= debíamos, 'we ought (not) to have'": the tense now named (imperfect
    indicative 1st pl., old ending -iemos = -íamos).
13. 2691–2693 · n · style. "the Infantes now cross the same country going north" → "going the other way, so that
    Atienza, on the Çid's right then (v. 415), is on their left now".
14. 2714–2717 · n · style. The arras "of vv. 2563–2570" → "of vv. 2564 and 2570", the two lines that name them
    (published 124–125).
15. 2684–2685 · l, n · style. "that-[him]self": the restored s is the whole reflexive, so "that-[himself]"; the note
    now cites *Grádanse* (gradarse, v. 172) for the verb.

Checked and confirmed, no change:
- **Rubric of 128** and its English; assonance "ó / ó-e"; 129 "í-a"; 130 "á-o".
- **2675–2676**: printed after 2680 at the head of 128 with ”¿ (continuation mark), as the note says; the order
  "in the manuscript after v. 2674" follows from Pidal's numbering.
- **que[s] grade (2685)**: s italic on the image; gradar(se) is the poem's verb (v. 172, glossary *grádanse*, *gradó*);
  present subjunctive optative 'may he be glad' is right; the dark irony is the rubric's.
- **[a nombre] (2705)**: both words italic, no note; "[in great number]" kept, marked not certain.
- **Griza / Álamos / Elpha / caños (2694–2695)**: no footnote on p. 296 (notes 2683, 2687, 2692, 2693, 2697, 2698
  only); the drafter's statement is true. *alu[o]n* (2696) and *ca[d]e*: italics as printed.
- **[nos] (2725)**: italic with the !; 'we', emphatic repeated subject, as *seremos nos* 2728, *prendemos nos* 2730.
- **sin cosimente (2743)**, **marridas (2750)**, **ensayandos (2746)**, **páranlas en cuerpos (2721)**, **enssienplo
  (2731)**, **comidieron (2713)**, **deportarse (2711)**, **los de criazón (2707)**, the long note to 2703, and the
  notes to 2752, 2754, 2759-60: quoted exactly as printed.
- **Twin series (129)**: the rubric's *(Serie gemela.)* and the note to 2752 (2749–50 like 2720–21) are reported
  correctly; the one-line explanation is ours and fair.
- **Cross-references**: lion vv. 2280 ff. (published: the lion gets loose at 2282, the episode from 2278); rogadores
  vv. 2079–2080 (published v. 2080, the king asks all present to be *rogadores*); Colada and Tizón v. 2575; barragán
  v. 2671 — all right.
- **House renderings**: Infantes, Doña Elvira in `i` (don Elvira in `l`), the Jalón, the Ansarera, "play at arms" for
  *tener armas*, Ruy Díaz, Diego and Fernando, San Esteban (as v. 396), Colada, Tizón, *amor* "love" (of husbands to
  wives, not a lord's favour), *vistas* "meeting".
- **Remembered translation**: none found; the `i` follows the grammar and Pidal's glosses.

## Pass 2: gloss.json

1. cosimente · error. Glossed 'sense, consciousness … perhaps from consentimiento', against Pidal's note
   (probablemente 'sin fuerzas, agotadas') and the unit. Rewritten from Pidal.
2. marridas · error. 'forlorn, afflicted … perhaps afligidas' — Pidal: generally 'afligido, apenado', here
   'desmayado'. Rewritten with both, the here-sense 'fainting' first.
3. duradores · error. "masc. pl." with *çinchas*: an adjective in -dor, one form for both genders. Fixed (= duraderas).
4. tajadores · error. Same fault with *espadas*. Fixed.
5. enssienplos · error. 'example, precedent … such evil examples' against Pidal 'hecho notable, acción' and the unit
   ("wicked deeds"). Rewritten.
6. asant · error. 'to San … aSant Estevan "to San Esteban"': the a marks the place-name object of *dexan* ('they leave
   San Esteban'), as *a Griza* v. 2694. Rewritten.
7. grade · weak. "= agrade; sense inferred, perhaps also 'be grateful'", unsourced etymology: the verb is the poem's
   gradarse (*Grádanse* v. 172). Now "gradar + se — may he be glad … = se alegre".
8. griza · weak. "perhaps Ariza (Zaragoza) by the usual identification" — not from Pidal (no note here), and an outside
   identification. Dropped; now only what the line says.
9. corpes · weak. "site not certainly identified, … south of the Duero" replaced by Pidal's note to 2697 (disappeared,
   south-west of San Esteban de Gormaz).
10. deviemos · weak. "imperfect/conditional … exact tense uncertain": imperfect indicative, old -iemos; fixed.
11. déxanlas · weak. Example "they leave them forlorn" → "fainting" (Pidal 'desmayado').
12. assomas · weak. Example gloss "it would be so if the Cid might appear then" → "what fortune it would be if the Cid
    appeared then".
13. ívanse · weak. The se belongs with *alabando* (iban alabándose); said so.
14. __broaden__ torna · weak. "does not give him an answer": the other is a lady; now "gives her no heed, no answer".
15. __broaden__ recabdo · weak. Same "him"; example now *el una al otra nol torna recabdo*, sense from context.
16. __broaden__ dar · weak (added). Known 'give, yield' does not cover *les conpieçan a dar* 'begin to strike them'.
17. __broaden__ montes · weak (added). Known 'mountain' does not cover 'woods' (vv. 2698, 2715, 2757 in the units).
18. __broaden__ monte · weak (added). *las aves del monte* 'the birds of the forest'.
19. __broaden__ fieras · weak (added). Known 'great, mighty' does not cover *bestias fieras* 'wild beasts'.
20. __broaden__ bestias · weak (added). Known 'beast, mount (riding/pack animals)' does not cover wild beasts.
21. __broaden__ cuerpos · weak (added). *en cuerpos*, Pidal 'las dejan a cuerpo'.
22. __broaden__ nombre · weak (added). *[a nombre]* 'in plenty', marked uncertain as in the unit.
23. altos, fieros · style. Examples said 'mountains'; now 'woods', as the units.
24. criazón, comidieron, briales, parejas, ensayandos · style. Pidal's own glosses added ('sus familiares …',
    'meditaron', 'el brial o ciclatón', 'iguales nuestras', 'esforzándose'); 'trying each other' dropped.
25. cortandos · style. Parallels *dándoslas* v. 2081, *indos* v. 832 added.
26. ronpien · style. "-ién" → "-ie ending" (printed unaccented).
27. __broaden__ con · style. 'up to, among … sense perhaps' → 'up to, as high as', with Pidal 'suben hasta las nubes'.

The drafter's broadens of *ques*, *irá*, *sabor*, *por*, *sobre*, *nos*, *vos*, *cade* are correct (old entry kept
whole). The rest of the 95 were checked against the form and found right. gloss.json parses; its keys equal the
novel-form tokens plus `__broaden__` (now 18), and every broaden begins with the known entry exactly + " · "
(verified by script).

## Refused

- 2725 `i` "— we beg you!" for the restored *[nos]*: the repeated verb is not in the line, but a bare "we!" is not
  English; the doubled "we beg you" carries the emphatic pronoun fairly. Kept.
- 2736 *tan sin sabor* "most cruelly": the literal sense is in the note; kept.
- *çiclatones* "silken tunics" in `i`, where v. 2572 has "silk brocade": here the word is the garment (Pidal, note to
  2721, *el brial o ciclatón*), there the cloth. Kept.
- *prendemos* (2730) `l` "we-take", `i` "suffer": the gloss has 'receive … perhaps suffer'; consistent enough. Kept.
- A broaden of *linpia* for "clear spring" / "clean blood": 'clean, pure' covers both. Not added.
- *aluon* lemma *alueñe*: a real old form; kept.
- Changing "Pidal has moved these two lines" (2675–2676): the inference from his numbers is sound and the previous
  part says the same. Kept.

## Left uncertain

- *[a nombre]* (2705): 'in plenty, in great number' taken; Pidal restores both words without a note.
- *caños* (2695) 'caves, underground passages', and the story of Álamos, Elpha and Griza: no note from Pidal; who shut
  up whom is the simplest reading only.
- *çinchas corredizas* (2736): 'running' girths, exact sense unknown; *tan sin sabor* 'so cruelly'.
- *nol torna recabdo* (2756): 'neither gives the other heed', from context.
- *cortandos* (2728): imperative with metathesis (cortadnos) taken; secure by the parallels but not noted by Pidal.
- Italic extent of Ati[en]ça (2691) and nu[ov]es (2698): read again at zoom 5 — e, n and o, v look italic, ç roman;
  agrees with the pin.
